title: Fallback profile table
description: A derived lookup table: for each configuration where a security property was measured to be LOST, the weaker configuration where it was measured to survive -- or one of the two words that say no such measurement exists. Produced by compiler/driver/tools/derive-fallback-table.mjs from a security-configuration envelope. NOTE ON VALIDATORS: this schema uses `if`/`then`/`else`, which compiler/driver/lib/jsonschema.mjs deliberately does not implement (it refuses unknown keywords rather than guessing). The conditional is the point of the document -- it is what stops a row saying `fallback` while pointing at nothing -- so it is written in draft-07 here and checked by a validator that implements it.

source.description: The envelope this table was derived from, pinned by content hash. A table whose source hash no longer matches the envelope on disk is stale, not merely old.

policy.description: The search rule, stated in the artefact rather than only in the code that made it. `fixedAxes` are the axes a fallback may not touch: moving target, ndebug, freestanding or cc produces a different program or a different environment, and moving lto both changes a whole-programme link decision this per-translation-unit recompile cannot make and moves along an envelope label that fuses a build flag with an observation stage (observe-config.sh gives full-prelink and full-backend the same compiler invocation). Either way that is a different experiment, not a fallback.

controlCells.description: Cells excluded from the search population because their cellId carries `ctl=`: positive controls for the observer's silent-failure modes. Excluded, counted here, and listed individually in `anomalies`.

lostCellsUnderBrokenInstrument.description: Cells reporting state=LOST while measurement says the instrument was broken or the configuration unsupported. They are a statement about the instrument, not about the property, so they get no row and are listed individually in `anomalies`. The same cell would be refused as evidence on the candidate side.

byState.description: The envelope tally carried through so the table can be reconciled against it without opening the envelope. `state` is about the property and `measurement` is about the instrument; they are counted apart because they are stored apart.

byMeasurement.description: The envelope tally carried through so the table can be reconciled against it without opening the envelope. `state` is about the property and `measurement` is about the instrument; they are counted apart because they are stored apart.

anomalies.description: Everything the derivation refused to throw away: excluded control cells, non-monotonic survival, fallbacks the current driver mechanism cannot express, duplicate cells. An empty array is a claim, not a default.

opt.description: A rung of the weakening ladder. `to` is a recommendation the driver will act on, so it may only name a level the ladder ranks.

resolution.description: Three words that must not be collapsed into two. `no-safe-target` is a positive claim about a complete set of measurements; `not-observed` is the admission that the set is incomplete. Merging them turns 'we did not look' into 'there is nothing there'.

rejectedItem.description: Why one candidate configuration was not adopted, for one subject. `measured-lost` and `measured-absent` are both observations and are different observations: LOST means the property was there and the toolchain removed it, ABSENT means it was never emitted. `not-observed`, `broken-measurement`, `unsupported` and `absent-from-envelope` are statements about the instrument or about coverage, never about the property.

lostSubjects.description: Every subject of this property that was measured LOST at `from`. A property carried by two programs can lose it in one and keep it in the other; both are named here rather than folded into the property.

then.description: A row that says `fallback` must name the configuration and the profile, and must cite at least one held cell per subject. Without this branch the word `fallback` could be written over a null.

else.description: `no-safe-target` and `not-observed` are both refusals to name a target, so both must leave `to` and `profile` null and cite nothing. A non-null `to` under either word would be a recommendation with no measurement behind it.

opt.description: The level the sweep compiled this cell at. Not restricted to the ladder: an envelope may hold -Os or -Og, and a row about such a cell resolves to not-observed rather than being dropped.
